citeAs: Li, Xinhao, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, and Limin Wang. (2025). VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv.
creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (Shanghai AI Laboratory; Nanjing University; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shanghai Innovation Institute)
description: LongVid is a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset introduced in the paper. It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types to support models in handling diverse long video scenarios.
name: LongVid
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: LongVid is built by leveraging existing datasets and captions, filtering consecutive segments that can be regrouped into a long video sequence, constructing event labels with timestamps, directly using existing event-level annotations where available, extracting major events from captions with an LLM for other datasets, and then constructing long-video QA pairs based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps. The resulting QA pairs are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset construction intentionally leverages a mix of source datasets spanning movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild long videos to increase diversity. However, LongVid is still curated from four existing open-source datasets, so its content distribution is shaped by those source datasets and their domains.
rai:dataCollection: LongVid is curated from four open-source video datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. The authors use existing short-video captions and event annotations from these sources, filter consecutive segments to reconstruct long videos, build timestamped event-label sequences, and generate QA pairs for five long-video task types.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data for LongVid are long-duration videos and associated captions/annotations drawn from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData, covering movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states that one challenge in long video model training is the shortage of large-scale, high-quality data, and notes that existing long-form video-text pair datasets lack the instruction-following paradigm of (video, instruction, answer) triplets crucial for multimodal reasoning. This limitation motivates the construction of LongVid.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The authors filter consecutive short-video segments that can be regrouped into long video sequences, concatenate or regroup captions into dense descriptions, extract major events from captions with an LLM when needed, construct timestamped event-label sequences, and synthesize multiple QA task formats from captions, event labels, and timestamps.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing includes filtering consecutive segments to reconstruct long videos; directly using high-quality event-level annotations when available; extracting major events from captions with an LLM for other datasets; concatenating lower-level captions into dense captions for some sources; and organizing captions and timestamps into long-video QA pairs.
rai:dataUseCases: LongVid is intended for long video instruction tuning and to support models in handling diverse long video scenarios. The QA pairs support five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: The construction uses an LLM to extract major events from captions for datasets without high-quality event-level annotations. In the appendix, the paper also states that an open-source LLM, Qwen-72B, is used to extract event and background labels from MiraData captions.
